title: The Theory of Forms
text:
Plato posited that the physical world experienced through sensory perception is merely an imperfect reflection of a transcendent realm containing perfect, unchanging blueprints of reality, known as the Forms. These Forms—such as Justice itself or Beauty itself—exist independently of human thought and constitute true being.

The Theory suggests that knowledge derived from mutable sense experience (opinion) cannot attain genuine understanding because it is constantly changing and particular to specific instances. True knowledge (*episteme*), conversely, can only be achieved through intellectual apprehension of these eternal, immutable Forms, which serve as the ultimate objects of study.

Accessing this realm requires rigorous philosophical training and utilizing the dialectical method. This approach aims to reconcile differing concepts and draw insights toward universal truths, thereby differentiating mere appearance from ultimate reality.
